claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 16 years old, his eligibility depends on what he's currently doing. Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they remain in approved education or training.

Could you tell me what Alex is currently doing? For example, is he:
- Still in full-time education (such as school or college)?
- In approved training?
- Working?
- Something else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in school anymore. He finished his GCSEs and decided not to continue with any further education or training. He's just at home at the moment, not really doing anything.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex is 16 and has left education, there's one more thing that could potentially help with eligibility.

Has Alex registered with any of the following since leaving education:
- A government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service in England, Careers Wales, Skills Development Scotland, or the Careers Service in Northern Ireland)?
- The armed services?

If a 16 or 17 year old registers with one of these services, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. He just finished school and has been at home since then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK, and yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just one more question to ensure I have the full picture:

Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more a week, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all, and he's not receiving any benefits in his own right.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK ✓
- Alex lives with you ✓
- Alex is 16 years old
- Alex has left education and is not in approved training
- Alex has **not** registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- Alex is not working or receiving benefits in his own right

Unfortunately, because Alex is 16 and has left approved education or training, you would normally only continue to qualify for Child Benefit if he had registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services (which would allow payments to continue for up to 20 weeks).

Since Alex hasn't done this, I'm afraid you would not currently be eligible for Child Benefit for him.

**However**, if Alex were to register with a government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service), you could then apply for Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks. This might be worth considering if Alex is looking for work or thinking about his next steps.

Let me record this outcome for you now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I've completed my assessment. To summarise:

**Outcome for Alex: Not Eligible**

You are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex because he is 16 and has left approved education or training without registering with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

**What you could do:**
If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service, you may be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks. This could be beneficial while he decides on his next steps, whether that's finding work, returning to education, or exploring other options.

Is there anything else you'd like me to help clarify?
